function: OTFS delay-Doppler channel estimation (PnP-CE, learned encoder-decoder denoiser) and symbol detection (PnP-SD, learned MLP denoiser) in a plug-and-play framework (p. 1-2, 8-9).
system: Single-antenna OTFS link, no RIS: N=20 time slots, M=20 subcarriers, 4QAM, 3 GHz carrier, 7.5 kHz spacing, speeds 135-405 km/h (p. 10, 13).
method: Plug-and-play ADMM with offline-trained denoisers: residual encoder-decoder CNN (estimation), MLP with soft mapper (detection); MSE on noisy/clean pairs, called unsupervised (p. 1, 7).
data_channel: Own Monte-Carlo simulation: P=5 paths, random delay and Doppler indices, CN(0,1/P) gains, kmax=3, lmax=4; 90,000 train and 10,000 validation samples, noise 0-50 dB; 2,000 test realizations (p. 10).
test_conditions: Offline training on 90,000 Monte-Carlo samples, noise 0-50 dB; tested on 2,000 realizations over SNR, integer/fractional Doppler, P=3-5; train-test channel mismatch not stated (p. 10-11).
baselines: CE: LS, LMMSE, HQS, EM-SBL, ADMM and learned CDRN [13]. Detection: LS, LMMSE, MPA, OAMP, all non-learned. Sequential CE+detection pairs (p. 10-12).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR (estimation); BER versus SNR and versus normalized CSI error (detection); convergence over iterations; running time (p. 10-13).
complexity: Table I: PnP-SD online O(M^3 N + I_L sum z_(l-1) z_l), 0.0028 s; offline training 518.27 s; none reported for the PnP-CE network (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 10: "the associated delay and Doppler indices for each channel path are randomly selected from" [0, lmax] and [-kmax, kmax], with CN(0, 1/P) gains, and "we generate the dataset using the Monte-Carlo method". Custom delay-Doppler simulator; no 3GPP TDL/CDL, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: dataset generated with "The number of channel paths is P = 5" and noise 0-50 dB; p. 2: "maintains robustness across diverse channel conditions without requiring retraining"; p. 11: "variations in the number of paths have only a limited influence". Missing: the paper never states which channel conditions the denoiser was trained on versus tested on in Figs. 8-9; the other sweeps are SNR and CSI error.
q3_support: p. 10: "the convolutional deep residual network (CDRN) [13]" as learned baseline next to LS, LMMSE, HQS, EM-SBL and ADMM; p. 11: "the proposed PnP-CE consistently outperforms all baselines across the entire SNR range" (NMSE, Fig. 7). Detection baselines LS, LMMSE, MPA and OAMP are all non-learned.
q4_support: p. 9: "As shown in Table I, the complexity" of the PnP-SD detector "in one iteration is expressed as" a Big-O expression; p. 10: Table I "Computational Complexities and Running Times of Different Algorithms" gives the PnP-SD online time (0.0028 s). No cost is given for the PnP-CE network.
q5_support: p. 10: "we generate the dataset using the Monte-Carlo method"; synthetic data from the paper's own simulator, with no link to code or data, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: Included, area 4 (OTFS delay-Doppler channel estimation and detection with learned PnP denoisers); the single-antenna link is admitted for OTFS (p. 13), no RIS. The PDF header reads accepted for publication, author's version, although it is labeled published. q1=0: custom delay-Doppler simulator. q2=0 is borderline: robustness across integer and fractional Doppler and P=3-5 without retraining is claimed (p. 2-3, 11), but the training channel conditions are never stated, so a train-test mismatch is not explicit; the reviewer should confirm. q3=1 rests on CDRN for estimation, while detection has only non-learned baselines. q4=1 from Table I for PnP-SD only; the EDN of PnP-CE has no cost reported. q5=0: synthetic data, no link. Table I and Figs. 7-9 were checked on PDF page 10.
